info.name: Restful-Booker API
info.description: API tests for the public Restful-Booker service (https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com). The suite creates its own booking and never asserts a fixed id or a fixed list size. Auth stores the token from POST /auth and sends it back as a Cookie header named token. A collection pre-request also requests a token when a folder is run on its own. Quirks of the live API are asserted on purpose and called out in the request scripts.

exec: // Grab one auth token per run and reuse it as Cookie: token={{token}}.
// Requests that must stay unauthenticated simply omit that header.
// basicAuth is the documented alternative: the API compares Authorization
body: { mode: "raw", raw: JSON.stringify({ username: user, password: pass }) }
console.warn("Auth pre-request did not return a token");
pm.test("Response time is under 20 seconds", function () {

item.name: Booking

request.description: Creates a booking owned by this run. A successful create returns 200, because the route uses res.send.

exec: // Quirk: create returns 200. The route calls res.send(record), whose default status is 200.
pm.test("Response matches the created-booking schema", function () {
pm.test("Response echoes the booking that was sent", function () {

request.description: Reads the booking created in this run. Accept is application/json.

exec: pm.test("Response matches the booking schema", function () {
pm.test("Stored booking matches the create payload", function () {

item.name: List bookings by first and last name

request.description: Filters by the unique name from this run. The assertion checks that the new id is present and does not expect a fixed list length.

exec: pm.test("Response matches the booking-id list schema", function () {
pm.test("The booking created in this run is in the filtered list", function () {

request.description: checkin is the day before the stored check-in and checkout is the day after the stored check-out. The handler uses $gt and $lt against an ISO timestamp, so the wider window is what matches. The firstname keeps the assertion independent of other public rows.

exec: pm.test("Response matches the booking-id list schema", function () {
pm.test("The wider date window includes the booking created in this run", function () {

request.description: Passing the booking's own check-in date does not return it. The firstname is unique to this run, so the list is empty.

exec: // Quirk: the apidoc describes check-in as "greater than or equal". The handler filters with
// Stored values are YYYY-MM-DD, and that string sorts before YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000Z,
// so the check-in day itself is excluded. firstname is unique to this run.
pm.test("Response matches the booking-id list schema", function () {
pm.test("Exact check-in date returns no rows for this guest", function () {

request.description: The parser accepts application/json, application/xml, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and */* only. text/html becomes 418.

pm.test("Body is I'm a Teapot", function () {

item.name: Negative
item.description: Unknown ids use the path segment does-not-exist so they cannot collide with a real numeric booking. Quirk creates are deleted before the folder ends.

item.name: Get a booking that does not exist

request.description: GET of an unknown id returns 404.
firstname alone fails validation. POST maps that failure to 500. additionalneeds is not a required field.

exec: // Quirk: a validation failure on POST /booking is 500. The same kind of incomplete
// body on PUT is 400 (see the incomplete full-update request). Required fields are
// firstname, lastname, totalprice, depositpaid, bookingdates.checkin, and bookingdates.checkout.
pm.test("Body is Internal Server Error", function () {

request.description: A truncated JSON body is rejected by the JSON parser with 400.
Validation runs before the id lookup, so an incomplete PUT body is 400 even when the id does not exist.

exec: // Quirk: PUT validation failure is 400, while POST validation failure is 500.
